clue.text: Lusty blokes kicking out Bernard (and charter) from the county

definitions.note: bucks are dashing, sexually eager young men

indicators.note: kicking out means throwing parts of the county's name out of it

parts.note: Buckinghamshire, the English county
Bernard Ingham, Margaret Thatcher's press secretary
to charter a boat or plane is to hire it

explanation.surface: Randy local men throw a man named Bernard, and some charter, out of their county.
explanation.walkthrough: Take INGHAM and HIRE out of BUCKINGHAMSHIRE and what is left is the county's usual short form. Bernard Ingham was Thatcher's famously gruff press secretary.
explanation.definitionFit: A buck is an old word for a spirited, amorous young man, as in young bucks.

clue.text: Withdraw whip in retaliation

parts.note: to back off or back out is to withdraw
a lash is a whip

explanation.surface: Pull back the whip to strike in revenge.
explanation.definitionFit: A backlash is a strong hostile reaction, a striking back against something.

clue.text: It facilitates movement without moving

definitions.meaning: the movement is a bowel movement, not travel
the user need not walk to a toilet

explanation.walkthrough: Movement suggests transport; it means a bowel movement, made in a chair-toilet by someone who cannot get to the lavatory.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a chair with a hidden chamber pot, used by the bedridden or infirm.

clue.text: Spread legs and knock off Penny inside?

indicators.note: inside puts the coin's letter within the killing word

parts.note: to knock off someone is slang for killing them

explanation.surface: A suggestive instruction about a woman spreading her legs and a penny.
explanation.definitionFit: To splay limbs is to spread them wide apart.

clue.text: After orgasm act like a scrubber and tell all

indicators.note: After puts the scrubbing piece behind the climax piece in the answer

parts.note: come is slang for reaching orgasm
a scrubber cleans; the surface plays on the slang sense of a loose woman

explanation.surface: A seedy confession: after sex, a woman of easy virtue spills everything.
explanation.walkthrough: Scrubber is British slang for a promiscuous woman, but here it just means someone who scrubs.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is an idiom for confessing everything you have been hiding.

clue.text: Bit of an arse's drug

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the cleft between the buttocks

explanation.walkthrough: Arse is British for backside.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names the gap between the buttocks and a smokable form of cocaine.

clue.text: Without a G. Adams, IRA collapses — about right time to celebrate!

indicators.note: about means the jumble goes round the right letter
collapsing letters fall into a new order
without means one letter a is dropped from the name and initials

parts.note: Gerry Adams, Sinn Féin leader
taken as written
taken as written: the single letter a

explanation.surface: Without Gerry Adams, the IRA falls apart, which is cause for a party.
explanation.walkthrough: Gerry Adams led Sinn Féin, the IRA's political wing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrove Tuesday, the last day before Lent, is a carnival festival in New Orleans and elsewhere.

clue.text: Love sex (not alfresco) so concede

parts.note: chuck is a Northern English term of endearment like love
it is a coy word for sex
alfresco is outdoors, so not alfresco is in

explanation.surface: Having sex indoors means giving in.
explanation.definitionFit: Chuck it in is British slang for giving up, admitting defeat.

clue.text: Saying "Ecstasy, Babe" and stuff

parts.note: Babe is the pig in the 1995 film
to ram something is to stuff it in

explanation.surface: Someone says ecstasy, babe, and so on.
explanation.walkthrough: E is slang for the drug ecstasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, witty saying.

clue.text: Tony's aide bungled (it's done away with execution by drowning in France)

indicators.note: bungled means the letters are botched into a different order
done away with says the letters of it's are removed from the pool

parts.note: the letters I, T, S as written

explanation.surface: A Blair aide's blunder is slipped away, like an execution in revolutionary France.
explanation.walkthrough: Take TONYSAIDE, remove I, T, S, and rearrange what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Noyade was the mass drowning of prisoners at Nantes during the French Revolution's Terror.

clue.text: Charles' first of the morning: getting off with one's royal consort

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word Charles

parts.note: Charles, the then Prince of Wales
a.m. marks the hours of the morning
feeling off means feeling unwell
one is A, as in a single thing

explanation.surface: Prince Charles, first thing in the morning, sleeping with his royal partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Getting off with suggests a sexual encounter; here it only joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Camilla Parker Bowles, later Queen Camilla, became the wife and consort of the then Prince Charles.

clue.text: "Come together — again" (Fry getting tossed outside European place of study)

indicators.note: outside means the jumbled letters wrap round the rest
tossing the word Fry jumbles its letters, like food in a pan

parts.note: taken as written
a uni is a university, British slang

explanation.surface: Stephen Fry gets thrown out of a European university campus.
explanation.walkthrough: Fry looks like the comic Stephen Fry or a cooking verb; it is just three letters to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To reunify is to bring divided parts, such as a split country, back into one whole.

clue.text: Nuts! Toilet! Pee! Baby's bottom!

parts.note: loo is British slang for a toilet
pee is how the letter P is spoken

indicators.note: the bottom of the word Baby is its final letter

parts.note: the possessive of baby, so the letters are those of baby

explanation.surface: A string of potty-training exclamations about a baby's backside.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are informal adjectives for someone who is crazy or mad.

clue.text: Briefly clad and exhausted, one's knocked off by Italy's premier

indicators.note: the letter for one is knocked off and the new one takes its place

parts.note: knackered is British slang for exhausted
one is A

indicators.note: premier means first, so only the opening letter of Italy counts

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone half-dressed and worn out, with an Italian prime minister doing the knocking off.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a single changed letter turns being worn out into wearing knickers.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearing knickers means being dressed in briefs, so the definition is a pun on brief clothing.

clue.text: (& 15ac./17/21) "Employment minister's wife had orgy!" "Nothing in it!" "Resign from power!"

definitions.meaning: the scandalous headline that forces a minister out
the official denial issued as he goes
what the minister actually does, under the usual excuse

annotation.spelling: SPEND MORE TIME WITH ONE'S FAMILY

explanation.surface: A tabloid scandal, a denial and a forced resignation, told in three shouted lines.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase was famously given by Norman Fowler, once Employment Secretary, when he left Thatcher's cabinet, and became the standard cover story for a politician quitting in disgrace.
explanation.definitionFit: Politicians who quit under a cloud traditionally claim they want to devote themselves to home life.

clue.text: They'd read Drunk? — Dry Out!

indicators.note: drunk letters stagger into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Drunks told by a sign to dry out, as in quit drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: To dehydrate is to remove water from something, drying it.

clue.text: (see13ac.)
Bloke getting married in Fergie's outfit

definitions.note: Sir Alex Ferguson managed this football club

parts.note: a bloke is a man
a married couple are united

explanation.surface: A man wears Sarah Ferguson's dress to his wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: Fergie suggests Sarah Ferguson, Duchess of York, and outfit clothing; it is Alex Ferguson and his team.
explanation.definitionFit: Manchester United is the football club Ferguson managed for decades, commonly shortened in speech.

clue.text: Traditional pirate's gear gets organ on the beat

indicators.note: on places the organ before the beat in the down answer

parts.note: the eye is a sense organ
a policeman's beat is his patch

explanation.surface: A pirate costume with an organ playing in rhythm.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage pirates traditionally wear a cover over one missing eye.

clue.text: (see 13ac.)
Since getting screwed lives without cuts

indicators.note: without means the living word goes outside the rest

parts.note: is means exists or lives

indicators.note: screwed letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Since being cheated, a person lives without circumcision.
explanation.definitionFit: To incise is to cut into something, as a surgeon does.

clue.text: Its fillings not savoury — pointless as a ginger biscuit

indicators.note: pointless drops a compass point, here south

parts.note: a ginger snap is a crisp biscuit, so snappy is like one

explanation.surface: A complaint that some biscuit's filling is sweet, not savoury, and the biscuit is dull.
explanation.walkthrough: A nappy (British for a diaper) is filled with something nobody would call savoury.
explanation.definitionFit: A baby's diaper gets filled with waste, which is the opposite of an appetising savoury filling.

clue.text: Po, wee Po, Teletubbies' no. 1

parts.note: to wee is to urinate
a po is a chamber pot

explanation.surface: Po the Teletubby is wetting itself.
explanation.walkthrough: Po is both a chamber pot and a Teletubby; a number one is a wee, and the rest of the clue plays on that.
explanation.definitionFit: A po is a British word for a chamber pot kept under the bed.

clue.text: (see 13ac.)
Refreshing desiccant for repeated pissing of one's pants?

indicators.note: refreshing the letters of desiccant renews their order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A drying agent recommended for someone who keeps wetting themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: Wetting yourself is politely called having an accident, so several such episodes are accidents.

clue.text: Like some free melons? (e.g. about $2000)

indicators.note: about means the example word goes round the money

parts.note: say introduces an example like e.g.
two grand, each grand being G

explanation.surface: Breasts let loose, worth two thousand dollars.
explanation.walkthrough: Melons is slang for breasts; free means without a bra.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsupported breasts hang low, so they are described as drooping.

clue.text: 'Fabulous author' Archer's main recoiling affectation

indicators.note: the main or leading letter of Archer is the first one

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: recoiling sends the word for affectation backwards

parts.note: a pose is an affected manner

explanation.surface: Jeffrey Archer, the novelist, mocked for his self-regarding airs.
explanation.walkthrough: The quote marks jab at Jeffrey Archer, a novelist jailed for perjury and so a teller of fables.
explanation.definitionFit: The ancient Greek storyteller is famous for fables such as the tortoise and the hare.

clue.text: Jam jar involved in castration

indicators.note: the car is involved in, tucked within, the word castration

parts.note: the letters run on in the middle of the word castration

explanation.surface: A jam jar used in a castration.
explanation.walkthrough: Jam jar is Cockney rhyming slang for car; the answer is a Vauxhall model.
explanation.definitionFit: The Vauxhall Astra is a popular British family car.

clue.text: Mo's "Stupid nit" buttonholing point to Brown

definitions.note: mo is British slang for a moment, as in half a mo

indicators.note: the muddled letters buttonhole, or grab and hold, the rest inside them
stupid letters are muddled, so nit is rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
S, south, is a compass point
tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Mo Mowlam calls Gordon Brown a stupid nit while cornering him.
explanation.walkthrough: Mo looks like Mo Mowlam, the Labour minister; it is slang for a brief moment.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean a very short time, as in wait a mo or wait an instant.

clue.text: Decline owner of round beer belly?

parts.note: an owner has got the thing
O is round in shape
a pot is a paunch, often from beer

explanation.surface: A sad decline into owning a round beer gut.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that a man who lets himself go ends up with a paunch, so the idiom and its literal reading match.
explanation.definitionFit: To go to pot is an idiom for deteriorating through neglect.

clue.text: Eye: dead artsy? Perhaps, but not now

indicators.note: perhaps hints the letters could be arranged otherwise

parts.note: taken as written
d. is short for dead in records
taken as written

explanation.surface: Private Eye mocks itself as an arty magazine whose time has passed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yesterday is the day before today, so it is a time that has passed, unlike the present.

clue.text: HRH finally gives one a teasing desire

definitions.note: the last letter of HRH, as a spelt-out word

parts.note: A is one
an itch is a nagging urge

explanation.surface: A royal teasingly offers someone something they crave.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the name of the letter that ends HRH.
explanation.definitionFit: This is how the letter H is spelt out in words, as in dropping your aitches.
